rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-fulk means ships, and the same form can denote one vessel or many.
rows.anchor: والفلك التي تجري في البحر يعني السفن واحدة وجمعه سواء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Masculine agreement follows the singular form and feminine agreement the collective sense.
rows.anchor: فالتذكير على الفظ الواحد والتأنيث على معنى الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ships benefit people by carrying riders and trade, livelihoods, and other goods sought.
rows.anchor: بما ينفع الناس يعني ركوبها والحمل عليها في التجارات والمكاسب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water sent down from heaven is rain.
rows.anchor: وما أنزل الله من السماء من ماء يعني المطر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth was revived after its dryness and barrenness.
rows.anchor: فأحيينا به الأرض بعد موتها بعد يبوستها وجدوبتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Batha means to spread and scatter.
rows.anchor: وبث نشر وفرق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The changing of winds means turning them into easterly, westerly, northerly, and southerly winds.
rows.anchor: وتصريف الرياح أي يقلبها قبولا ودبورا وشمالا وجنوبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is that God turns the winds between mercy and punishment.
rows.anchor: تصريفيها مرة بالرحمة ومرة بالعذاب

rows.speaker: حمزة والأعمش والكسائي وخلف
rows.claim: These readers recite الريح in the singular; the remaining readers use the plural الرياح.
rows.anchor: الريح بغير ألف على الواحد وقرأ الباقون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas associates plural winds with mercy and the singular wind with punishment.
rows.anchor: الرياح للرحمة والريح للعذاب

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to pray that a blowing wind be made plural winds of mercy, not a singular wind of punishment.
rows.anchor: اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word الريح can be grammatically masculine or feminine.
rows.anchor: والريح يذكر ويؤنث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Clouds are called sahab because they move as if dragging themselves along.
rows.anchor: سمي سحابا لأنه يسحب أي يسير في سرعته كأنه يسحب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are indications that let rational people know these things have a creator and maker.
rows.anchor: لقوم يعقلون فيعلمون إن لهذه الأشياء خالقا وصانعا

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet warns of woe for anyone who recites this verse without reflecting and learning from it.
rows.anchor: ويل لمن قرأ هذه الآية فمج بها

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators identify the rivals people take besides God as idols worshipped apart from Him.
rows.anchor: ومن الناس من يتخذ من دون الله أندادا يحبونهم يعني الأصنام المعبودة

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the rivals are chiefs obeyed in disobedience to God, and their love resembles believers' love of God.
rows.anchor: ساداتهم وقاداتهم الذين كانوا يطيعونهم في معصية الله

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars take the comparison to mean that idolaters love the rivals as believers love God, an ellipsis comparable to saying one sale is like another's sale.
rows.anchor: يحبونهم كحبهم الله يعني أنهم يسوون بين هذه الأصنام

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra cites a poem whose comparison omits the understood speaker, supporting the elliptical construction of the love comparison.
rows.anchor: ولست مسلما ما دمت حيا

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Abi Ablah reads فعدة in the accusative, with an understood command to fast the missed number of days.
rows.anchor: فعدة نصبا أي فليصم عدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The missed days are other than the days of illness or travel; أخَر is genitive but indeclinable because it is shifted from أواخر or أخريات.
rows.anchor: من أيام أخر غير أيام مرضه أو سفره والعدة العدد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعائشة وعطاء بن رباح وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة ومجاهد
rows.claim: They read يطيقونه with the described vowel and consonant changes, explaining it as being able to bear the fast.
rows.anchor: يطيقونه بضم الياء وبفتح الطاء

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعكرمة
rows.claim: They also transmit a reading meaning that people take the fast upon themselves with effort.
rows.anchor: أيضا يطيقونه بفتح الياء وتشديد الطاء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas is reported to read a further form with the meaning of يطيقونه; طاق, أطاق, and أطيق are equivalent forms.
rows.anchor: وروى ابن الأنباري عن ابن عباس يطيقونه بفتح الياء الأول

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة والشام وأبو عمرو ومجاهد
rows.claim: They read فدية طعام مساكين with an annexed phrase; singular الطعام can be annexed to plural مساكين because the two words differ in form.
rows.anchor: فدية طعام مضافا مساكين جمعا أضافوا الطعام إلى الفدية

rows.speaker: نافع عن ابن عمر ومجاهد
rows.claim: A report transmits the plural مساكين reading from Ibn Umar, and Mujahid is also reported to read it.
rows.anchor: طعام مساكين على الجمع، وروى مروان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reads فدية منصوبًا with طعام مرفوعًا and مسكين singular in the genitive.
rows.anchor: فدية منصوبة، طعام رفعا، مسكين خفض

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد وأبو حاتم
rows.claim: They prefer the plural reading, which distributes the food among the whole group; the singular reading means one poor person for each day.
rows.anchor: ومن جمع رده إلى الجميع

rows.speaker: عيسى بن عمر ويحيى بن وثاب وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read يتطوع with an imperfect verb and geminated ط; the others read تطوع as a past verb.
rows.anchor: يتطوع بالتاء وتشديد الطاء وجزم العين

rows.speaker: بعض العلماء
rows.claim: One view says the choice between fasting and feeding was the first Ramadan rule, then 2:185 abrogated the feeding option; authorities include Muadh, Anas, Salama, Ibn Umar, and others, plus one Ibn Abbas report.
rows.anchor: كان ذلك أول ما فرض الصوم وذلك أن الله تعالى

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع بن أنس وسعيد بن جبير عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They say the feeding concession applied to elderly men and women and others burdened by fasting, then was abrogated except for those unable to fast.
rows.anchor: بل هو خاص للشيخ الكبير والعجوز الكبيرة والذين يطيقان الصوم

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan applies the original choice to any sick person, even one still able to fast, until the rule was abrogated.
rows.anchor: هذا في المريض كان إذا وقع عليه اسم المرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On these interpretations the verse is abrogated, which the author says is the view of most jurists and commentators.
rows.anchor: الآية منسوخة وهو [قول] أكثر الفقهاء المفسرين

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب والسدي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Another view says no part was abrogated: those once able to fast but later incapacitated feed the poor, and the verse remains operative.
rows.anchor: لم تنسخ هذه الآية ولا شيء منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author treats يطيقونه from الإطاقة as the sound reading used by most Qur'an readers and regional codices, while variant يطوقونه was interpreted for the elderly and incurably ill.
rows.anchor: فحمله ما ذكرنا من هذه الأقاويل على قراءة من قرأ يطيقونه

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء وطاوس والسدي
rows.claim: They explain فمن تطوع خيرا as adding food for more than one poor person.
rows.anchor: فزاد على مسكين واحد وأطعم مسكينين فصاعدا

rows.speaker: ابن جريج وخطيف عن مجاهد
rows.claim: They explain the phrase as giving more than the required amount of food.
rows.anchor: فمن زاد على القدر الواجب من الإطعام

rows.speaker: ابن شهاب
rows.claim: Ibn Shihab says the better course is to fast as well as provide the food.
rows.anchor: يريد فمن صام مع الفدية وجمع بين الصيام والطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fidya means compensation or a substitute, as in giving one thing in place of another.
rows.anchor: الجزاء والبدل من قولك: فديت هذا بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author classifies Ramadan breakers into four groups: owing both make-up and expiation, make-up alone, expiation alone, or neither.
rows.anchor: لا رخصة لأحد من المؤمنين البالغين في إفطار شهر رمضان إلا لأربعة

rows.speaker: ابن عمر ومجاهد والشافعي
rows.claim: Those who delayed make-up until the next Ramadan, and pregnant or nursing women fearing for their children, owe both make-up and expiation; if they fear for themselves, they follow the sick person's rule.
rows.anchor: هذا قول ابن عمر ومجاهد ومذهب الشافعي

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: For a pregnant or nursing woman fearing for herself and her child, Ibn Abbas says expiation is due without make-up.
rows.anchor: أن عليهما الكفارة ولا قضاء وهو قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والحسن وعطاء والضحاك وأهل العراق ومالك والأوزاعي
rows.claim: They require make-up but no expiation for pregnant or nursing women who fear for themselves or their children.
rows.anchor: ولا كفارة وهو قول إبراهيم والحسن وعطاء والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sick, traveler, menstruating woman, and woman with postpartum bleeding owe make-up but no expiation.
rows.anchor: فالمريض والمسافر والحائض والنفساء عليهم القضاء دون الكفارة

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that the Prophet said travel waives fasting and half of prayer.
rows.anchor: قال أنس: أتيت إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The elderly, those with incurable chronic illness, and people with dangerous thirst owe food expiation but no make-up, according to most jurists.
rows.anchor: فالشيخ الهرم والشيخة الكبيرة ومن به مرض دائم لا يرجى برؤه

rows.speaker: ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن وخالد بن الدريك
rows.claim: They say elderly people who cannot fast owe nothing; Malik does not consider expiation obligatory but recommends it.
rows.anchor: وروى عن ربيعة بن أبي عبد الرحمن وخالد بن الدريك إنهما قالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The insane person owes neither make-up nor expiation.
rows.anchor: فأما الذي لا قضاء عليه ولا كفارة فالمجنون

rows.speaker: أهل العراق
rows.claim: One view sets food expiation at half a sa for each missed day.
rows.anchor: نصف صاع عن كل يوم يفطره وهذا قول أهل العراق

rows.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
rows.claim: Another view sets half a sa of wheat or a full sa of dates, raisins, or other grains.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم منهم: نصف صاع من قمح أو صاع من تمرا

rows.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
rows.claim: A further view measures the food by what the person normally eats for a day.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الفقهاء: ما كان المفطر يتقوته يومه

rows.speaker: محمد بن الحنفية
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Hanafiyya prescribes a mudd of food and a mudd of its accompaniment for every day.
rows.anchor: وقال محمد بن الحنفية (رضي الله عنه) : يطعم مكان كل يوم مد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says to give one poor person the evening meal at sunset and the predawn meal before dawn.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: يعطي مسكينا واحدا عشاءه حين يفطر

rows.speaker: ابن هريرة وعطاء ومحمد بن عمرو بن حزم والليث بن سعيد ومالك بن أنس والشافعي
rows.claim: These jurists prescribe one mudd of food for one poor person per day.
rows.anchor: وهو قول ابن هريرة وعطاء ومحمد بن عمرو بن حزم

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading puts شهر رمضان in the nominative, understood as a new clause such as أتاكم شهر رمضان.
rows.anchor: شهر رمضان قرأه العامة رفع على معنى أتاكم شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: الفراء والأخفش والكسائي
rows.claim: They offer different omitted predicates for the nominative reading: that is Ramadan, it is Ramadan, or fasting Ramadan was prescribed.
rows.anchor: الأخفش: هو شهر رمضان. الكسائي: كتب عليكم شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد وشهر بن حوشب
rows.claim: They read شهر رمضان in the accusative, interpreted as an instruction to fast the month; other grammarians analyze it as temporal adverbial or exhortative.
rows.anchor: شهر رمضان نصبا على هو يعني صوموا شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr assimilates the two adjacent r sounds in شهر رمضان for ease of articulation.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو عمرو: مدغما شهر رمضان على مذهب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word شهر is tied to notoriety; al-Farra also derives it from whiteness, with examples of unsheathing a sword and the moon appearing.
rows.anchor: هو مأخوذ من الشهرة وهي البياض ومنه يقال

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One opinion treats Ramadan as a name of God, supporting the wording month of Ramadan; a report from Ja'far al-Sadiq's forebears attributes that phrase to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: رمضان اسم من أسماء الله فيقال شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: أنس عن هشيم عن أبان
rows.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says not to say Ramadan alone but to call it the month of Ramadan as the Qur'an does.
rows.anchor: لا تقولوا رمضان، انسبوه كما نسبه الله تعالى في القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو
rows.claim: Abu Amr says Ramadan was named because good deeds are scorched in it.
rows.anchor: إنما سمي رمضان لأنه رمضت فيه الفعال من الخير

rows.speaker: غيره
rows.claim: Other explanations connect Ramadan with hot stones, the burning away of sins, or hearts being heated by admonition and reflection on the afterlife.
rows.anchor: لأن الحجارة كانت ترمض فيه من الحرارة والرمضاء الحجارة المحماة

rows.speaker: الخليل
rows.claim: Al-Khalil derives Ramadan from autumn rain, saying it washes bodily sins and purifies hearts.
rows.anchor: مأخوذة من الرمض وهو مطر يأتي في الخريف فسمي هذا الشهر رمضان

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains that the Qur'an descended whole from the Preserved Tablet on Ramadan's Night of Decree to the lower heaven, then Gabriel brought it to Muhammad in stages over twenty years.
rows.anchor: أنزل القرآن جملة واحدة من اللوح المحفوظ في ليلة القدر من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Sha'bi says Gabriel reviewed the year's revelations with Muhammad in Ramadan, confirming, retaining, or causing him to forget what God willed.
rows.anchor: في رمضان ما نزل الله

rows.speaker: أبو ذر الغفاري
rows.claim: A report lists revelation dates for Abraham's scrolls, the Torah, Gospel, Psalms, and Qur'an as successive nights in Ramadan.
rows.anchor: أنزلت صحف إبراهيم في ثلاثة ليال مضين من رمضان

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: Salman's report of the Prophet's end-of-Sha'ban sermon calls Ramadan a blessed month containing a night better than a thousand months, with fasting obligatory and night prayer voluntary.
rows.anchor: سلمان قال: خطبنا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في آخر يوم من شعبان

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: The sermon promises extraordinary reward for good deeds and obligations, calls Ramadan a month of patience and generosity, and says believers' provision increases.
rows.anchor: من تقرب فيه بخصلة من خصال الخير كان كمن أدى فريضة

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: The sermon says the month's beginning brings mercy, its middle forgiveness, and its end release from the Fire; feeding a fasting person earns forgiveness and an equal reward.
rows.anchor: شهر أوله رحمة وأوسطه مغفرة وآخره عتق من النار

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: The Prophet says even a sip of milk, a date, or water earns the feeding reward; a full meal earns a drink from his basin without thirst until Paradise.
rows.anchor: من فطر صائما على مذقة لبن أو تمر أو شربة ماء

rows.speaker: سلمان
rows.claim: The sermon urges easing a slave's work and seeking four practices: testimony and repentance to please God, and asking for Paradise and refuge from Hell.
rows.anchor: فيه من أربع خصال: خصلتان ترضون بها ربكم

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that heaven and Paradise gates open on Ramadan's first night; each prayer earns a large reward, daily fasting brings forgiveness and a palace, and angels seek forgiveness for the faster.
rows.anchor: إن أبواب السماء وأبواب الجنة لتفتح لأول ليلة من شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: قتادة عن أنس
rows.claim: A report says the first night renews Paradise and closes Hell to Muhammad's community, chains rebellious devils, and frees servants from the Fire daily.
rows.anchor: إذا كان أول ليلة من شهر رمضان نادى الجليل جلت عظمته

rows.speaker: قتادة عن أنس
rows.claim: In the same report, a heavenly caller invites repentance, supplication, justice, forgiveness, and requests; God urges endurance throughout the month, and angels descend on Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: هل تائب يتاب عليه؟ هل من داع يستجاب له؟

rows.speaker: أنس عن إبراهيم بن هدية
rows.claim: Anas reports that if God let heaven and earth speak about someone who fasted Ramadan, they would say: Paradise.
rows.anchor: لو أذن الله للسماوات والأرض أن يتكلما بشرا بمن صام رمضان

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: The Prophet is reported to say that a faster's sleep is worship, silence is glorification, supplication is answered, and deeds are multiplied.
rows.anchor: نوم الصائم عبادة وصمته تسبيح ودعاؤه مستجاب

rows.speaker: العامة
rows.claim: The common reading of فليصمه has a jussive lam; Hasan and al-Araj read it with kasra, which is proper when the command lam is isolated, while connection permits either vowel.
rows.anchor: قرأه العامة بجزم اللام، وقرأ الحسن والأعرج: بكسر اللام

rows.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأصحابه
rows.claim: They interpret witnessing the month as being sane, adult, resident, healthy, and legally responsible, and therefore required to fast.
rows.anchor: معناها فمن شهده عاقلا بالغا مقيما صحيحا مكلفا فليصمه

rows.speaker: النخعي والسدي
rows.claim: They say anyone who enters Ramadan while resident must complete the whole month's fast, even if he later travels.
rows.anchor: إذا دخل عليه شهر رمضان وهو مقيم في داره فليصم الشهر كله

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says someone who meets Ramadan at home and then travels still has to fast.
rows.anchor: إذا أدركه رمضان وهو مقيم ثم سافر فعليه الصوم

rows.speaker: محمد بن سيرين عن عبيدة السلماني
rows.claim: Ubayda says that one who witnessed the month's beginning should fast its end; the view recommends not leaving home after Ramadan begins.
rows.anchor: إذا شهدت أوله فصم آخره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعامة أهل التأويل
rows.claim: The author says the sounder view is to fast while present and take the concession to break the fast when traveling; he cites the Prophet drinking during the Ramadan conquest journey.
rows.anchor: وهو أصح الأقاويل يدل عليه ما روى الزهري عن عبيد الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The Prophet's statement that fasting on a journey is not righteousness is contextualized by a man weakened in the shade; travelers are told to accept God's concession.
rows.anchor: ليس من البر أن تصوموا في السفر، وعليكم برخصة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The author applies the same context to the saying that a traveler fasting is like someone breaking the fast at home.
rows.anchor: الصائم من السفر كالمفطر في الحضر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar rebukes a man cooling his face while fasting on a journey and warns that dying in that condition would lead to the Fire.
rows.anchor: أفطر ويحك فإني أراك لو مت على هذا دخلت النار

rows.speaker: عمر بن عبد العزيز
rows.claim: Resolving Ibn Umar's and Aisha's differing practice, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz says to fast when travel is easy and break the fast when it is hard.
rows.anchor: إذا كان يسرا فصوموا وإذا كان عسرا فأفطروا

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وأنس وإبراهيم ومجاهد
rows.claim: One juristic view holds that fasting while traveling is preferable; Anas says those who break do so by dispensation, while those who fast have the better course.
rows.anchor: الصوم أفضل، وهو قول معاذ بن جبل وأنس وإبراهيم ومجاهد

rows.speaker: جعفر بن محمد عن أبيه عن جابر
rows.claim: Another view prefers breaking the fast: on the conquest journey the Prophet drank after people struggled, and called those who persisted in fasting disobedient.
rows.anchor: أولئك العصاة

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: On a hot journey, those who broke the fast watered the mounts while fasting companions collapsed, so the Prophet said the non-fasters took the reward that day.
rows.anchor: ذهب المفطرون اليوم بالأجر

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar likens rejecting God's travel concession to rejecting a charitable gift.
rows.anchor: فإنها صدقة من الله عز وجل تصدق بها عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The journey permitting a fast to be broken is sixteen farsakhs or more.
rows.anchor: وحد الاسفار التي يجوز فيها الإفطار ستة عشر فرسخا فصاعدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God wills ease by granting concessions to the sick and traveler.
rows.anchor: يريد الله بكم اليسر حين أرخص في الأسفار للمريض والمسافر

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر يزيد بن القعقاع
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far reads العسر and اليسر with heavier pronunciation throughout the Qur'an; the other readers use the lighter form, and both are good dialects.
rows.anchor: العسر واليسر مثقلين في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects using this verse as proof for the Qadariyya, because the passage specifically legislates fasting for Muslims.
rows.anchor: ولا حجة للقدرية في هذه الآية لأنها مبنية على أول الكلام

rows.speaker: أبو بكر ورويش
rows.claim: They read ولتكملوا with a geminated m; the remaining readers lighten it, which the author prefers in light of 5:3.
rows.anchor: قرأ أبو بكر ورويش: بتشديد الميم

rows.speaker: الزجاج وعطاء
rows.claim: The purpose clause means God made this easy so the fast may be completed; Ata specifies completing the days of the month.
rows.anchor: معناه فعل الله ذلك ليسهل عليكم ولتكملوا العدة

rows.speaker: سائر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators understand completing the number as making up days missed through illness or travel.
rows.anchor: ولتكملوا عدة ما أفطرتم في مرضكم وسفركم

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars understand magnifying God to mean reciting takbir on Eid eve.
rows.anchor: أراد به التكبير ليلة الفطر

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وزيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: They say Muslims should say takbir from sighting Shawwal's crescent until the imam arrives, then stop unless following his takbir; the preferred wording repeats it three times.
rows.anchor: إذا رأى هلال شوال أن يكبروا إلى أن يخرج الإمام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is to be magnified for guidance, enabling the faith, and granting Ramadan, which is a distinction from other religious communities.
rows.anchor: على ما هداكم لدينه ووفقكم ورزقكم شهر رمضان

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One interpretation takes الدعاء as obedience and God's answering as granting its reward when the person obeys Him.
rows.anchor: معنى الدعاء هاهنا الطاعة ومعنى الاجابة الثواب

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some restrict the general promise: prayers are answered only if God wills, accord with decree, avoid impossibility, or are beneficial; Abu Sa'id's report says a sinless, non-severing prayer receives one of three outcomes.
rows.anchor: أجيب دعوة الداعي إذا وافق القضاء

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد
rows.claim: The Prophet says a Muslim's prayer without sin or severing kinship brings an immediate answer, an afterlife reserve, or protection from equivalent harm.
rows.anchor: ما من مسلم دعا الله عز وجل بدعوة ليس فيها قطيعة رحم

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view treats the promise as general but guarantees an answer rather than fulfillment of the request; denying this would make God's report false, and reports from Ibn Umar and David support answered prayer.
rows.anchor: فأما إعطاء المنية وقضاء الحاجة فليس مذكور في الآية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Prayer has manners and conditions that occasion an answer; whoever observes them qualifies for a response.
rows.anchor: إن للدعاء آدابا وشرائط هي أسباب الاجابة

rows.speaker: إبراهيم بن أدهم
rows.claim: Ibrahim ibn Adham says prayers go unanswered because people know God and the Prophet without obeying or following the Sunna, neglect the Qur'an and gratitude, ignore the afterlife and death, and fixate on others' faults.
rows.anchor: لأنكم عرفتم الله فلم تطيعوه وعرفتم الرسول فلم تتبعوا سنته

rows.speaker: المفسرون
rows.claim: Initially, after iftar people could eat, drink, and have sex until the late evening prayer or sleep; afterward these were forbidden until the next night.
rows.anchor: كان الرجل في ابتداء الأمر إذا أفطر حل له الطعام والشراب والجماع

rows.speaker: عمر بن الخطاب
rows.claim: After having sex with his wife following the late prayer, Umar repented to the Prophet; other men confessed similar conduct, and the verse then permitted intimacy on fasting nights.
rows.anchor: إني رجعت إلى أهلي بعد أن صليت العشاء الاخيرة

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود والأعمش
rows.claim: They read الرفوث; both rafath forms are euphemisms for intercourse, and Ibn Abbas says God's Qur'anic terms for touching, meeting, and intimacy mean intercourse.
rows.anchor: الرفوث: إلى نسائكم والرفث والرفوث كناية عن الجماع

rows.speaker: القتيبي
rows.claim: Al-Qutaybi says rafath explicitly names what should be euphemized in sex talk and derives from obscenity or coarse speech.
rows.anchor: الرفث هو الإفصاح بما يجب أن يكنى به من ذكر النكاح

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-Ajjaj's verse uses rafath in speech, illustrating the term's association with coarse talk.
rows.anchor: أسراب حجيج كظم … عن اللغا ورفث التكلم

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines rafath as a comprehensive term for men's desires toward women.
rows.anchor: الرفث كلمة جامعة لكل ما يريده الرجال من النساء

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: The spouses are garments in the sense of being a place of rest and repose, as night is called a garment and a spouse is made for repose.
rows.anchor: هن لباس لكم وأنتم لباس لهن هن سكن لكم

rows.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
rows.claim: They explain the garment metaphor by spouses sleeping unclothed together, each body close against the other like an inner garment.
rows.anchor: اللباس الشعار الذي يلي الجهار من الثياب فسمي كل واحد من الزوجين لباسا

rows.speaker: النابغة بني جعدة
rows.claim: Al-Nabigha ibn Ja'da's poem calls a woman لباسا, supporting the metaphor for spouses joined in bed.
rows.anchor: تثنت وكانت لباسا

rows.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
rows.claim: Al-Rabi ibn Anas paraphrases the spouses as each other's covering blanket.
rows.anchor: هن لحاف لكم وأنتم لحاف لهن

rows.speaker: بعضهم وأبو زيد
rows.claim: Another view says each spouse covers the other from forbidden conduct and from public view during sex; Abu Zayd explains the phrase as referring to intercourse.
rows.anchor: يقال لما ستر الشيء وواراه لباس فجائز أن يكون كل واحد منهما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda says a wife may be called a man's garment, bedding, or waist wrap, as in a poem addressed to Umar.
rows.anchor: يقال للمرأة هي لباسك وفراشك وازارك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To betray oneself refers to wronging oneself with intimacy after the late prayer; God then forgave and erased their sins.
rows.anchor: تخونونها وتظلمونها بعد العشاء الآخرة في ليالي الصوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-an marks a time that spans both past and coming time, while bashiruhunna means have intercourse because skin touches skin.
rows.anchor: باشروهن جامعوهن حلالا سميت المجامعة مباشرة لتلاصق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ابتغوا means seek or do; ما كتب الله لكم means what God decreed or wrote in the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: قضى الله لكم، وقيل: كتب في اللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators understand what God ordained as offspring; Mujahid urges seeking children, while Ibn Zayd reads it as lawful intercourse.
rows.anchor: ابتغوا الولد إن لم تلد هذه فهذه

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands the phrase as seeking the concession God prescribed.
rows.anchor: ابتغوا الرخصة التي كتبت لكم

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل وأبو الجوزاء عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: They interpret what God prescribed as Laylat al-Qadr.
rows.anchor: ابتغوا ما كتب الله لكم يعني ليلة القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author prefers the offspring interpretation because it follows the permission of intercourse and is framed as permission or encouragement, supported by a Prophetic call to marry and multiply.
rows.anchor: وأشبه الأقاويل بظاهر الآية قول من تأوله على الولد

rows.speaker: أهل الظاهر
rows.claim: The literalists say the command to seek what God wrote is obligatory, citing a report about al-Hawla, who asks Aisha why her husband avoids intimacy.
rows.anchor: هو أمر إيجاب وحتم، يدل عليه ما روى زياد

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: In the al-Hawla report, the Prophet tells the wife to listen to and obey her husband, then promises merit for household care, pregnancy, labor, and nursing.
rows.anchor: اذهبي واسمعي له وأطيعي، فقالت: أفعل يا رسول الله

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: The continuation of the al-Hawla report promises men rewards for approaching, embracing, kissing, and having intercourse with their wives, and forgiveness through ritual washing.
rows.anchor: ما من رجل أخذ بيد امرأته يراودها إلا كساه نور

rows.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
rows.claim: Muadh identifies the Anṣari man in the dawn-food occasion as Abu Sirma, al-Bara Qays ibn Sirma.
rows.anchor: معاذ بن جبل: أبو صرمة البراء قيس بن صرمة

rows.speaker: عكرمة والسدي
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Suddi give his name as Abu Qays ibn Sirma.
rows.anchor: عكرمة والسدي: ابو قيس بن صرمه

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
rows.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan names him Sirma ibn Iyas.
rows.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان: صرمة بن أياس

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi gives the man's fuller genealogy as Abu Qays Sirma ibn Anas ibn Abi Sirma ibn Malik ibn Adi al-Najjar.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: أبو قيس صرمة بن أنس بن أبي صرمة بن ملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Anṣari fasted while working, slept before his wife finished preparing food, refused to eat after waking under the old rule, and fainted from exhaustion the next day; the revelation then allowed eating and drinking at night until dawn.
rows.anchor: فاغتم لذلك رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فأنزل الله تعالى وكلوا

rows.speaker: الشاعر
rows.claim: A poem likens dawn's beginning light to a white thread and the dark night to a black one.
rows.anchor: الخيط الأبيض وقت الصبح منصدع … والخيط الأسود لون الليل مكموع

rows.speaker: أبو داود
rows.claim: Abu Dawud's verse describes daybreak as a thread of light.
rows.anchor: ولاح من الصبح خيط أنارا

rows.speaker: عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: Adi ibn Hatim says he literally watched black and white hairs; the Prophet laughed and clarified the image as daylight against night.
rows.anchor: إنما ذلك بياض النهار من سواد الليل

rows.speaker: سهل بن سعد
rows.claim: Sahl reports that before من الفجر was revealed, some men used actual threads to judge when to stop eating; the added phrase clarified that night and day were intended.
rows.anchor: كان رجال إذا أرادوا الصوم يضع أحدهم في رجليه الخيط الأبيض والخيط الأسود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dawn is the first splitting of light, named from water bursting forth; the false dawn rises vertically without spreading, while the true dawn spreads across the horizon.
rows.anchor: والفجر انشقاق عمود الصبح وابتداء ضوءه

rows.speaker: سمرة بن جندب
rows.claim: The Prophet says not to stop eating because of Bilal's call or the vertical false dawn, but at the spreading dawn along the horizon.
rows.anchor: لا يمنعكم من السحور آذان بلال ولا الصبح المستطيل

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: The Prophet's party delayed iftar until sunset despite a companion's doubt; when night arrives, day recedes, and the sun sets, the faster has completed the fast whether or not he eats.
rows.anchor: إذا أقبل الليل من هاهنا وأدبر النهار وغابت الشمس فقد أفطر الصائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tikaf fundamentally means staying and residing; the cited Qur'anic phrase describes people remaining at idols.
rows.anchor: أصل العكوف والاعتكاف الثبات والاقامة

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line likens people gathered around cooking pots to people devoted around an idol, illustrating the root of i'tikaf.
rows.anchor: يرى حولهن معتفين كأنهم … على صنم في الجالية عكف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: I'tikaf is confining oneself in a mosque for worship of God.
rows.anchor: والاعتكاف هو حبس النفس في المسجد على عبادة الله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وعطاء والضحاك والربيع
rows.claim: They limit the prohibited intimacy of i'tikaf to intercourse, which invalidates the retreat.
rows.anchor: هي المجامعة خاصة معناه لا تجامعوهن ما دمتم معتكفين

rows.speaker: قتادة ومقاتل والكلبي
rows.claim: They report that some companions left the mosque during retreat to have sex with their wives, then bathe and return, and were forbidden intercourse day and night until retreat ended.
rows.anchor: نزلت هذه الآية في نفر من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كانوا يعتكفون

rows.speaker: أبو زيد
rows.claim: Abu Zayd takes direct intimacy broadly to include intercourse, touching, kissing, and other pleasures.
rows.anchor: المباشرة الجماع وغير الجماع من اللمس والقبلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Intercourse invalidates i'tikaf by consensus; pleasurable touching or kissing without intercourse is disliked but does not invalidate it for most jurists.
rows.anchor: والجماع مفسد للاعتكاف بالإجماع، والمباشرة غير الجماع

rows.speaker: مالك بن أنس
rows.claim: Malik holds that non-intercourse direct intimacy invalidates i'tikaf.
rows.anchor: مالك بن أنس: يفسده

rows.speaker: ابن جريج عن عطاء
rows.claim: Ata says the forbidden act is intercourse itself, though he dislikes even kissing or touching in the mosque.
rows.anchor: أما الذي حرم فالجماع وأنا أكره كل شيء من ذلك

rows.speaker: عائشة
rows.claim: Aisha reports that the Prophet, while in retreat, would extend his head out of the mosque for her to comb.
rows.anchor: كان يخرج إليها رأسه من المسجد فترجله وهو معتكف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس عن سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says a person in retreat is kept from sins and receives the reward of all good-doers.
rows.anchor: هو معتكف الذنوب وتجري له من الحسنات كعامل الحسنات كلها

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين عن أبيه
rows.claim: A Prophetic report promises the reward of two pilgrimages and two minor pilgrimages for ten days of Ramadan i'tikaf.
rows.anchor: من اعتكف عشرا في رمضان كان بحجتين وعمرتين

rows.speaker: السدي وشهر بن حوشب والضحاك
rows.claim: They gloss God's limits as His conditions, obligations, or prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قال السدي: شروط الله. شهر بن حوشب: فرائض الله. الضحاك: معصية الله

rows.speaker: المفضل بن سلمة والخليل والزجاج
rows.claim: They define a limit as a boundary or endpoint that distinguishes or prevents transgression; the author adds that the root means restraint and cites Arabic usage.
rows.anchor: وأصل الحد في اللغة: المنع ومنه قيل للبواب حداد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not approach the limits means do not commit the prohibited acts; God clarifies the signs so people avoid His anger and punishment.
rows.anchor: فلا تقربوها فلا تأتوها، يقال: قربت الشيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The dispute is an argument from proof; Nimrod ibn Canaan is identified as a tyrant who claimed divinity, and God granting him kingship explains his arrogance.
rows.anchor: خاصم وجادل وأصلها من الحجة، وهو نمرود بن كنعان

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says two believers ruled the earth—Solomon and Dhul-Qarnayn—and two disbelievers—Nimrod and Nebuchadnezzar.
rows.anchor: ملك الأرض مؤمنان وكافران، فأما المؤمنان فسليمان بن داود

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil dates the debate to after Abraham broke the idols, when Nimrod imprisoned him and prepared to burn him.
rows.anchor: لما كسر إبراهيم الأصنام سجنه نمرود ثم أخرجه ليحرقه

rows.speaker: آخرون
rows.claim: Other interpreters place the debate after Abraham had been thrown into the fire.
rows.anchor: آخرون: كان هذا بعد إلقائه في النار

rows.speaker: زيد بن أسلم عن معمر
rows.claim: A report says Nimrod controlled food distribution; when Abraham answered that God gives life and death, Nimrod sent him away without food, but God provided a fine meal from a sand dune he carried home.
rows.anchor: فرده بغير طعام فرجع إبراهيم عليه السلام إلى أهله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation says Nimrod rejected an angel's repeated call to believe, challenged God to battle, and his army was destroyed by mosquitoes; one entered his brain and tormented him for four hundred years, matching his reign.
rows.anchor: فأوحى الله عز وجل إلى خزنة البعوض أن افتحوا منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's answer to Nimrod responds to an unstated prior question: who is Abraham's Lord?
rows.anchor: تقديره: قال له: من ربك

rows.speaker: الأعمش وحمزة وعيسى
rows.claim: They read ربي with a quiescent ya; the other readers vocalize it with a fatha before the definite article.
rows.anchor: ربي الذي بإسكان الياء، وقرأ الباقون بفتحه

rows.speaker: أهل المدينة
rows.claim: Readers of Medina lengthen أنا throughout the Qur'an, treating connected speech like the original form; al-Kisai and another poet's verses attest the usage.
rows.anchor: أهل المدينة (أنا) بالمد في جميع القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The original أنا has an open n; its written alif represents pause, and many Arabs pronounce it with a final h at pause.
rows.anchor: والأصل في (أنا) أن تفتح النون وابتغي لها الوقت

rows.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
rows.claim: Most commentators say Nimrod called sparing one man and killing another giving life and death, with the same sense as 5:32's phrase about not killing a person.
rows.anchor: دعا نمرود برجلين فقتل أحدهما واستحيا الآخر فسمى ترك القتل إحياء

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says Nimrod starved four men, fed two near death, and let two die; Abraham then changed to the clearer proof of the sun rather than because he lacked a reply.
rows.anchor: أخذ أربعة نفر فأدخلهم بيتا فلا يطعمون ولا يسقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nimrod was bewildered, stunned, and cut off from argument.
rows.anchor: فبهت الذي كفر أي تحير ودهش وانقطعت حجته

rows.speaker: محمد بن السميقع اليماني
rows.claim: He reads فبهت with open b and h, meaning Abraham stunned Nimrod, supported by 21:97.
rows.anchor: محمد بن السميقع اليماني: فبهت بفتح الباء والهاء

rows.speaker: بعض نحاة البصرة
rows.claim: They attach أو كالذي to an implicit question about whether one has seen a case like the disputant or the traveler; some take the comparative kāf as extra.
rows.anchor: عطف على معنى الآية الأولى تقديره: هل رأيت

rows.speaker: قتادة والربيع وعكرمة وناجية بن كعب وسليمان بن بريدة والضحاك والسدي وسليم الخواص
rows.claim: These authorities identify the traveler as Ezra (Uzayr ibn Sharya).
rows.anchor: هو عزير بن شرحيا

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه وعبد الله بن عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: They identify the traveler as Jeremiah ibn Khalfiya, from Aaron's line, and connect him with al-Khidr.
rows.anchor: هو أرميا بن خلفيا وكان من سبط هارون ابن عمران

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the traveler was an unbeliever who doubted resurrection.
rows.anchor: مجاهد: هو رجل كافر شك في البعث

rows.speaker: وهب وعكرمة وقتادة والربيع
rows.claim: They identify the ruined town as Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: هي بيت المقدس

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak identifies the town as the Holy Land.
rows.anchor: الضحاك: هي الأرض المقدسة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the town was the place where thousands who feared death were destroyed after leaving their homes.
rows.anchor: الأرض التي أهلك الله فيها الذين خرجوا من ديارهم

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Al-Kalbi identifies the town as the monastery of Sa'idabad.
rows.anchor: الكلبي: هي دير سائداباذ

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies the town as Salmabad.
rows.anchor: السدي: هي سلماباذ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other suggested sites are the monastery of Harafil and the Grape Village, two farsakhs from Jerusalem.
rows.anchor: دير هرافيل، وقيل: قرية العنب وهو على فرسخين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khawiya can describe a collapsed house or an emptied house; ʿurush are roofs and buildings, and the verse means roofs fell first and walls on top of them.
rows.anchor: إن السقوف سقطت ثم وقعت الحيطان عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading takes على to mean with; a poem is cited for that usage, and analogous wording occurs in al-Kahf and al-Hajj.
rows.anchor: وقيل: (على) بمعنى مع، أي خاوية مع عروشها

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه عن محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: A long report identifies the traveler as Jeremiah: God chose and commissioned him to warn sinful Israel, inspired his sermon, and foretold a Babylonian destruction; Jeremiah pleaded not to witness it, and God made his consent the condition of their destruction.
rows.anchor: محمد بن إسحاق عن وهب بن منبه: إن الله سبحانه وتعالى

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه عن محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: The report continues: Jeremiah refused consent to Israel's destruction, told a pious king, and the king accepted the possibility of punishment for their sins or pardon through mercy; the people then persisted in wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: والذي بعث موسى بالحق لا أرضى بهلاك بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An angel twice posed as a wronged relative to Jeremiah, who urged him to treat his family well; during Babylon's siege, he later exposed their behavior as deserving God's anger.
rows.anchor: وقال: أنا الذي أنبأتك في شأن أهلي مرتين

rows.speaker: وهب بن منبه عن محمد بن إسحاق
rows.claim: After the king asked him to pray, Jeremiah asked God to spare Israel if righteous and destroy them if they persisted in wrongdoing; a heavenly lightning strike and ruined temple followed, and Jeremiah learned his own prayer had triggered it.
rows.anchor: إن كانوا على حق وصواب فابقهم وإن كانوا على سخطك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nebuchadnezzar conquered Jerusalem, killed Israelites, destroyed the temple, selected one hundred thousand boys, and divided the rest among those left in Syria, taken captive, and killed; this was the first punishment for their injustice.
rows.anchor: فكانت هذه الواقعة الأولى التي أنزلها الله ببني إسرائيل بظلمهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On returning to Jerusalem with grape juice and figs on his donkey, Jeremiah saw the ruins and asked how God would revive the town after its death.
rows.anchor: فلما ولى بخت نصر عنهم راجعا إلى بابل

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Those who say the traveler was Ezra place him among the Israelites deported to Babylon, alongside Daniel and seven thousand descendants of David.
rows.anchor: وقال الذين قالوا إن هذا المار كان عزيزا
